p4_fields.endpoint_pursued: A WWOX-linked lactate/LDH readout that a compound moves: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic human neural cells at matched maturity; then a locomotor, network or myelin endpoint.
p4_fields.functional_evidence_available: None for WWOX in humans. Fly: a single partial locomotor rescue by Ldh RNAi in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction genotype. Human knockout organoid: LDHA transcript up but confounded with maturity.
p4_fields.temporal_or_model_limit: Fly amyloid model, whole-head metabolomics, partial RNAi; the human row is a transcript.

cellular_context.target_expression: LDHA and LDHB are broadly expressed; LDHC is testis-restricted by convention and absent from the organoid expression universe.
cellular_context.cells_tissue_stage: whole fly head (glia carry the highest Wwox mRNA, so neuronal origin of lactate is not established); bulk organoid RNA.
cellular_context.limits: Lactate rises only with Wwox reduction plus amyloid and falls nominally without amyloid; one human MRS datum reports lactate extremely low.

mission_dimensions.track_definition: mission.md section 5: Track A = variant-independent WWOX loss of function; Track B = variant or allele-class specific (e.g. the Q230P missense class); Track C = repurposing, which is a method of reaching A or B, not a third lesion class
mission_dimensions.route_definition: RECUPERO_PROFONDO = deep recovery of the lost function; BENEFICIO_PRECOCE = concrete partial benefit, symptomatic control or protection of function, with paediatric feasibility and time in view
mission_dimensions.route_note: A downstream metabolic lever with one genetic precedent in a fly (partial locomotor benefit). Not deep recovery; WWOX function would remain lost. Track B (Q230P class): no allele-specific rationale; the lever is allele-blind and untested for any allele.
mission_dimensions.the_two_dimensions_are_independent: a card keeps both: a variant-independent lever can be a partial-benefit lever, and a lesion-specific one can aim at deep recovery

p4_card.identity: LDH-directed levers: stiripentol (approved for a paediatric developmental epilepsy; weak LDH inhibition in vitro), GSK2837808A and other research LDHA inhibitors, and the LDHA-directed oligonucleotide nedosiran (approved for primary hyperoxaluria, liver-directed). Per-compound table: compounds_and_sources.md section 2.2.
p4_card.indication_and_transfer: WWOX-DEE only IF lactate or LDH activity is shown to be a driver in a WWOX-deficient human neural system. The one fly precedent is amyloid-conditional; human lactate readouts in WWOX deficiency are normal or low in the cited sources (DL-BIO-008, DL-BIO-009).
p4_card.novelty_for_woree: NON_TROVATO_NELLA_RICERCA as a test: no source retrieved links an LDH inhibitor to WWOX deficiency; coverage is the six sources of compounds_and_sources.md and ten PubMed abstracts on 2026-10-26. The 2015 report usually cited for stiripentol and LDH in epilepsy was not found by my query and is not cited.
p4_card.state_of_known_roads: not in the earlier hand-made series; relates to map record N-06 (lactate as a readout) and HYP-20260709-01.
p4_card.pathway_and_objective: BENEFICIO_PRECOCE; Track A, Track B untested.
p4_card.expected_contribution: UNKNOWN. A partial locomotor benefit was seen once in the fly with Ldh RNAi; no human or WWOX datum.
p4_card.mechanism: Target: LDHA (HGNC:6535, P00338) and LDHB (HGNC:6541, P07195); direction: lower LDH activity or lactate production; context: amyloid-stressed fly head in the paper; UNKNOWN in WWOX-DEE. For stiripentol the LDH link is not the established basis of its antiseizure use.

external_not_wwox_evidence: ChEMBL activity rows for stiripentol and GSK2837808A
Open Targets: nedosiran as the only LDHA clinical candidate

for: Ldh RNAi improved climbing in the amyloid-plus-Wwox-reduction fly genotype (once).
Ldh transcript and lactate rise together in that genotype.
Stiripentol is an approved paediatric epilepsy drug with a nominal LDH link; nedosiran shows LDHA lowering is tolerated in humans in the liver.
against: The Ldh rescue lacks an Ldh-alone arm, a Wwox-mRNA check and a lactate readout, and the authors cite Ldh knockdown as detrimental in other fly amyloid models.
Without amyloid lactate falls nominally and Ldh does not change.
Stiripentol inhibits LDH only weakly in the measurements retrieved, and has other pharmacology; any benefit would not be attributable to LDH.
LDHA in the organoid is as consistent with immaturity as with WWOX loss.
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency is reported normal or extremely low.
evidence_for_and_against.transfer_limits: The fly effect needs amyloid; stiripentol's approved use depends on co-administration with another antiseizure drug and does not establish brain LDH engagement.

p4_card.time_to_access: UNKNOWN for research use; stiripentol is marketed for another indication (label retrieved, openFDA 2026-04-27).
p4_card.pharmacology: Stiripentol: marketed formulation with a paediatric label for Dravet syndrome with clobazam; weak LDH inhibition in vitro; brain LDH engagement not retrieved. GSK2837808A: potent on LDHA in vitro, no in vivo or CNS datum retrieved. Nedosiran: liver-directed.
p4_card.paediatrics_and_interactions: Stiripentol label: indicated for Dravet syndrome seizures in patients taking clobazam, from six months of age (openFDA label 2026-04-27); the same label means any use here would sit on top of clobazam co-therapy, an interaction this card does not assess. No paediatric suitability for WWOX-DEE is presumed.

scope_of_checks.support_and_replication: No independent replication of any fly row is held; the organoid rows are one laboratory's deposit.
scope_of_checks.formal_checks: Disease-side fly rows carry verbatim locators in the manifest (104 entries; entries 31, 49, 89, 94 SUPPORTED by a blind audit, entry 95 narrowed after an OVERSHOOT finding); the compound statements are abstract-level and unaudited.
scope_of_checks.card_inferences_owed_audit: Statements marked INFERENZA, including every statement about what a compound would do in WWOX-deficient tissue, are OWED a blind audit by another actor.

p4_card.next_measurement: In the fly: lactate (enantiomer- or isotope-resolved) in the Ldh-RNAi double genotype, an Ldh-alone arm, and Wwox mRNA in the double line. In human neural cells: LDH activity and the lactate-to-pyruvate relationship in WWOX-deficient versus isogenic cells at matched maturity. Only then a compound arm: stiripentol against a selective LDHA tool at matched exposure, so that its other pharmacology is separable from LDH.
p4_card.value_added: Separates the LDH lever into measured (fly, conditional), asserted (the Ldh-to-lactate step) and unmeasured (any human WWOX system), and records that the approved paediatric candidate inhibits LDH only weakly in the retrieved measurements.
p4_card.clinical_census: Clinical census, ClinicalTrials.gov API v2, 2026-10-20 (drug_repurposing/clinical_census_20261020.md): seven queries returned no registered WOREE interventional study; it answers seven queries against one registry on one date and a missing hit does not prove that no study exists. Not re-run for this card.

Whether stiripentol engages LDH in brain at tolerated exposures.
Whether Ldh lowering is beneficial or harmful without the amyloid context.
Why lactate falls nominally with Wwox reduction without amyloid.
evidence_against: Ldh knockdown is detrimental in other fly amyloid models (the authors' own citation).
Weak LDH inhibition by stiripentol in the retrieved measurements.
Human lactate in WWOX deficiency reported normal or extremely low.
bridge_gaps_exposed: Fly and organoid rows do not share a context, so no directional comparison is formed between them; the one fly-internal comparison (Ldh RNAi against Wwox knockdown on climbing) is a genetic, not a pharmacological, comparison.

card_conventions: IPOTESI throughout; the bridge forces it. No score, rank, probability or blended index is carried.

Abstract-level statements from PubMed are labelled abstract_only; none carries a receipt.
